REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - AUGUST 24, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
AUGUST 24, 2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Ryan Klement, Associate Pastor, New Life Community Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Bryant Ju, Cerritos resident selected to be part of the
  12 and under USA National Team – Baseball World Cup.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo

  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Pro Care Physical Therapy (Business Spotlight).

  Bryant Ju (Cerritos resident selected to be part of the 12 and under USA National Team –
  Baseball World Cup).

5B.  Review and consideration of appointments, removals, and filling of scheduled or unscheduled
  vacancies on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (2022-24 term) (COUNCIL).

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  There was no action taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Katarina Thompson requested traffic calming measures in the Pine Creek/Canyon Road
  area of the Granada Park Cerritos development.

  Samar Malouf requested traffic calming measures in the Pine Creek/Canyon Road area of
  the Granada Park Cerritos development.

  Paki Mat commented on various aspects of his personal beliefs.

  Paul Bellenbaum commented on various aspects of his experience in the Cerritos

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence submitted by the deadline listed on the agenda is considered

  unredacted written correspondence which was submitted for this item. Public requests for

  business hours to the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer).

  Katarina and Alfred Thompson and Samar and Stephanie Malouf requested traffic calming
  measures in the Pine Creek/Canyon Road area of the Granada Park Cerritos development.

  Andres Martinez Pais provided information on the California Mortgage Relief Program and
  offered his assistance to the City with regard to the program.

9A.  Review and consideration of renaming the Cerritos Library’s study rooms (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian and Marketing Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to direct staff to:

  1. Submit a budget amendment to increase the Professional Services account in the
  Municipal Library cost center (110-571-61430) in the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Combined
  Financial Program by $4,014.10 to cover the costs for new Study Room name signs
  and an online survey project; and

  2. Post an online survey for the community to vote for up to three (3) names of women,
  including the list of women and biographical information presented in the agenda report
  associated with this item; and

  3. Promote the opportunity to vote for Study Room names through a poster displayed in
  the library, on the library’s video wall, on the City’s social media channels, in the City’s
  newsletter, and on Cerritos TV3; and

  4. Report back to the City Council with the results of the vote with a recommendation to
  rename three (3) Study Rooms after the top three (3) vote-getters; and

  5. Conduct a drawing at the City Council meeting to randomly select the three (3) Study

  6. Award a contract to TFN Architectural Signage for the fabrication and installation of the
  new Study Room signs at an estimated cost of $3,546.10 (COUNCIL).

12.  Closed Session (continued)

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT:

  The City Council reconvened into Open Session.

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, provided the following announcements concerning items
  considered in Closed Session:

  Item Nos. 12A and 12B:  The City Council continued its deliberations as part of the
  City Manager recruiting process, and no reportable action
  was taken on either of these two items.

  Item 12C:  The following action was reported:

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Authorize the City’s special counsel, Colantuono Highsmith & Whatley (Special
  Counsel), and the City Attorney to negotiate a settlement agreement that would
  include a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) covering specified covenants between
  Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) and the City relating
  to the expansion of Metro’s West Santa Ana Branch rail line into Cerritos, and
  authorizing the Mayor to sign the MOU if a signed MOU from Metro included those
  specified covenants. Because Cerritos did not have a final or signed MOU from Metro at
  that time, this item was not required to be reported out at the August 10, 2023
  meeting, as negotiations on the settlement of the case were still pending.

  On August 24, 2023, Special Counsel and the City Attorney’s Office received from
  Metro a signed Settlement Agreement and MOU from Metro, and the MOU includes the
  specified covenants between Metro and the City relating to the expansion of the West
  Santa Ana Branch rail line into Cerritos. Therefore, pursuant to the City Council’s prior
  action, the City and Metro have reached a settlement of this case by City Council’s
  approval of the signed MOU and Settlement Agreement.

  The substance of the settlement may be summarized as follows: (1) per the MOU,
  Metro covenants to work with the City on a future study, budget, parking
  requirements, and other specified covenants set forth in the MOU relating to a
  potential future station located in Cerritos in the vicinity of 183rd Street and Gridley
  Road; and (2) the City agrees to dismiss with prejudice this existing litigation, brought
  against Metro for alleged violations of the Public Records Act, with no party having to
  pay any monetary contribution to the other, each party agreeing to cover their own
  litigation costs, neither party admitting any liability or fault, and other standard terms
  and conditions for settlement (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on the next page)

12.  Closed Session (continued)

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT (continued):

  Item 12D:  The following action was reported:

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Authorize seeking an appeal by filing a petition for review in the California Supreme
  Court of the recent opinion issued by the Second District Court of Appeal. This case
  may be summarized as follows: The petition for writ of mandate was brought by
  Orange County Council of Governments (OCCOG) and several Southern California
  cities, including Cerritos. The writ of mandate sought to set aside the Regional Housing
  Needs Assessment (RHNA) allocation of 1,341,827 dwelling units, as determined by
  the State Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD), for the
  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) region, change input data,
  and re-calculate the SCAG regional housing need. The trial court sustained demurrers
  filed by HCD and SCAG, which argued that judicial review is not available under the
  RHNA process. Sustaining the demurrers effectively dismissed the petition, and
  judgment was entered in favor of HCD and SCAG, and against the petitioners. OCCOG
  and the several cities, including Cerritos, per prior City Council authorization, noticed
  an appeal of this trial court ruling. The Court of Appeal recently filed an opinion,
  affirming the trial court’s decision.

  By the action taken by the City Council tonight, Cerritos will continue to be a co-
  appellant to the lawsuit and has authorized Special Counsel, Aleshire & Wynder LLP, to
  file a petition for review of the Court of Appeal opinion (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Item 12E:  The City Council was updated on the status of the appeal for this case and
  no reportable action was taken on this item.

  City Attorney and City Clerk/Treasurer performance evaluations) for discussion and there
